Summary



The US Medical Affairs Director, Governance serves as the governance lead and operations transformation architect for US Medical Affairs Medical operations strategy. The role designs and implements integrated operating models across Medical Governance, Clinical Drug Supply, Medical Operations, and other capabilities, translating strategy into scalable structures, governance, decision rights, roles, processes, handoffs, performance measures, and enabling tools that drive high performance and operational effectiveness.

Working across US Medical Affairs and key partner functions, the Director aligns stakeholders, manages dependencies and risks, resolves challenges and bottlenecks, manages risk mitigation, leads continuous change evolution, orchestrates inter-dependencies, proposes design and performance improvements, and strengthens execution, accountability, and measurable value realization. The Director leads stakeholder management and sustained adoption, using organization design, AI, analytics, technology enablement, capability building, and continuous improvement to embed new ways of working at scale.


This position can be based remotely anywhere in the U.S. (there may be some restrictions based on legal entity). Please note that this role would not provide relocation as a result. The expectation of working hours and travel (domestic and/or international) will be defined by the hiring manager. This position will require 20% travel.

About the Role

Key Responsibilities

Strategy & Operations Effectiveness

  • Design, implement, and continuously improve cross-functional operating models across Medical Governance, Medical Operations, Clinical Drug Supply, and other assigned USMA capabilities.
  • Translate strategic priorities into executable plans with clear scope, governance, decision rights, milestones, dependencies, resources, risks, performance measures, and implementation requirements.
  • Assess current-state processes, identify root causes of delay or fragmentation, and implement practical improvements across functions and teams.
  • Establish consistent operating standards for intake, prioritization, handoffs, service expectations, escalation, issue resolution, documentation, and performance review, adapting them to each function’s needs.
  • Lead the implementation and evolution of the USMA Medical Governance framework, including governance forums, risk and CAPA oversight, audit readiness, annual health checks, decision documentation, dashboards, and leadership reporting.
  • Build organizational effectiveness within the Medical Operations team through operating model refinement, role clarity, objective setting, coaching, performance management, talent development, succession planning, resource allocation, and accountability for delivery.
  • Partner with Clinical Drug Supply to strengthen forecasting, planning, ordering, packaging, labeling, distribution, inventory visibility, vendor coordination, issue escalation, and supply continuity across Medical Affairs studies and programs.
  • Orchestrate inter- dependencies across contracts, drug supply, clinical operations, governance, finance, procurement, legal, quality, and compliance to enable integrated execution and earlier issue resolution.

Transformation Architecture & Enablement

  • Architect enterprise and cross-functional transformations by defining the case for change, future-state vision, operating model, design principles, capability requirements, transformation roadmap, and value measures.
  • Translate strategy into integrated transformation blueprints that align people, process, governance, technology, data, decision rights, and ways of working across organizational boundaries.
  • Establish the transformation governance needed to sequence initiatives, manage dependencies and risks, resolve design tradeoffs, and maintain alignment from concept through implementation.
  • Design scalable implementation approaches, playbooks, decision frameworks, dashboards, and enabling tools that convert transformation intent into executable and repeatable ways of working.
  • Orchestrate adoption across U.S., global, and operational delivery teams through stakeholder alignment, role clarity, capability building, technology enablement, communications, and leader-led change.
  • Track transformation outcomes, adoption, and value realization; use performance insights to refine the architecture, accelerate implementation, and sustain impact over time.

Strategic Partnership & Culture

  • Serve as a strategic thought partner to functional leaders by translating complex operational challenges into clear options, recommendations, decisions, implementation plans, and measurable outcomes.
  • Influence senior leaders and cross-functional stakeholders to align priorities, resolve tradeoffs, and strengthen enterprise-wide accountability.
  • Promote a culture of enterprise thinking, proactive problem-solving, shared ownership, continuous improvement, and cross-functional collaboration.

AI, Digital & Analytics Enablement

  • Model and promote responsible, effective use of artificial intelligence across the team, embedding AI into workflows and fostering experimentation, learning, and adoption.
  • Use AI, automation, analytics, collaboration platforms, and digital workflow tools to streamline work, improve decisions, and increase quality and efficiency.
  • Partner with technology, privacy, legal, compliance, quality, and business stakeholders to implement fit-for-purpose digital solutions with appropriate governance and controls.

Position Requirements

Education & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in business, supply chain, operations, technology, life sciences, or a related field required; advanced degree preferred.
  • Ten or more years of progressive experience in the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, healthcare, supply chain, or another highly regulated industry.
  • Proven experience leading strategy, transformation, organizational effectiveness, or capability development in a complex matrix environment; consulting or agency experience preferred.
  • Demonstrated success designing and implementing complex cross-functional operating models and large-scale transformation or operational excellence initiatives through sustained adoption.

Expertise & Capabilities

  • Broad knowledge of Medical Affairs operations, including governance, contracting, vendor management, clinical drug supply, quality, compliance, risk management, audit readiness, and evidence generation.
  • Experience diagnosing organizational and operational effectiveness and translating findings into clearer roles, decision rights, processes, systems, technology, stakeholder engagement, and team-level solutions.
  • Strong program and project leadership capabilities, including planning, prioritization, dependency management, risk management, implementation, and value realization.
  • Advanced ability to synthesize quantitative and qualitative data, external evidence, and stakeholder insights into executive-level recommendations and decisions.
  • Experience developing practical operating tools, dashboards, trackers, service measures, capacity models, decision frameworks, and governance mechanisms.
  • Advanced AI and digital fluency demonstrated through recognized certification, applied experience, or a portfolio of AI-enabled solutions that improved decisions, workflows, capabilities, or measurable outcomes.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence senior leaders and cross-functional stakeholders in a highly matrixed organization without relying on direct authority.
  • Strong executive communication, facilitation, problem-solving, negotiation, and stakeholder-management skills.
  • Ability to operate collaboratively and transparently in a highly networked, fast-moving environment.
  • Sound judgment in balancing speed, quality, compliance, supply continuity, stakeholder needs, and business priorities while maintaining accountability for outcomes.
  • Intellectual and technical curiosity, with a commitment to continuous learning and practical application of emerging tools and practices.

The Role

As our Security Engineer, Application Security, you will own the security of the software we build — our cloud services, APIs, data pipelines, and the applications that run across our distributed, edge-deployed systems. You will be the security partner engineering teams turn to: leading threat models and design reviews, finding and helping fix vulnerabilities in code, and steering the architecture of our products toward secure-by-default.

This is a hands-on senior role with broad autonomy. You’ll go deep on code and architecture, build the tooling and automation that scales application security across a fast-moving engineering org, and raise the security bar through developer enablement rather than gatekeeping. You will work closely with Engineering, our security operations team, and GRC, and help shape the secure software development lifecycle as the company grows.

Overview

The Manager, Grant Writing & Partnership Communications is part of Y-USA’s fundraising team and supports the organization’s ability to reach and sustain its annual fundraising goal in service to organizational priorities through the writing and on-time submission of high-quality funding proposals and other related documents. This role is responsible for coordinating and providing guidance and tools related to the writing and coordination of grant applications and the development of proposals and donor reports. This team member supports the entire organization as a lead writer on their grant efforts and is responsible for written articulation of funding cases for Y-USA’s organizational priorities. This includes letters of inquiry, proposals, concept papers, white papers, case statements, donor reporting, some presentation materials, and other documents as assigned. This position is responsible for managing all stages of the proposal development process for assignments within assigned portfolio, including any required research and cross-departmental collaborations to secure content.

The Financial Development department secures and sustains the philanthropic resources that power the organization’s mission on a national scale. Connecting donors and their resources directly to transformative programs and people at both Y-USA and the local community level, the department leads comprehensive fundraising strategies across corporate and foundation partnerships, individual giving, major and principal gifts, and planned giving. Through strong donor relationships, data driven practices, and cross organizational collaboration with YMCAs across the country, Financial Development aligns philanthropic investment with strategic priorities, driving urgent and measurable impact in service to millions of individuals and families every day. Its work ensures the organization’s long-term financial strength not only for today but for years to come

YMCA of the USA (Y-USA) embraces a remote-first working environment which means most employees work remotely from a home office within the continental United States.

Responsibilities

  • Write and manage approval of public and private partnership applications among all departments, including gathering supporting materials, in accordance with Y-USA and partner requirements.
  • Write and manage approval of all written documents (within assigned portfolio) needed to contribute to annual fundraising goal for organizational priorities (e.g., grant applications, proposals, concept papers, case language, donor reports, letters of inquiry, etc.), assuring adherence to style guide parameters, Y brand, voice, and compliance requirements.
  • Manage coordination of all assigned proposal and report development activities across all Y-USA departments
  • Ensure funding proposals and reporting (including photos, media samples, etc.) is compliant with donor format/standards.
  • Maintain a working knowledge of Y strategies, priorities, and historical initiatives to connect work across initiatives, departments, and partner communications
  • Synthesize various initiative inputs through meetings, briefs, prior proposals, etc. to develop a robust written or visual expression Y-USA strategies and initiatives.
  • Responsible for donor reporting including narrative and data input. Coordinate with Manager, Financial Development Data & Budget on donor budget reporting.
  • Lead coordination across Y-USA staff members across departments to obtain necessary project updates for partnership reports.
  • Design and develop visual presentation materials for partner proposals and reports
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

EFFECT ON END RESULTS/STRATEGIC IMPACT

As the YMCA advances our ambitious new national strategy and ten-year vision of change—to improve individual and community wellbeing by intentionally strengthening connection and belonging—this is an exciting and critical moment to join our national office at Y-USA. This specialized role offers a meaningful opportunity for a highly-skilled and passionate candidate to contribute to nation-wide impact by supporting the ongoing success of the Y’s national strategic plan. Through compelling, fact-based storytelling, the grant writer will help communicate Y-USA’s strategic priorities across diverse and ever evolving projects, programs, and subject areas. Translating vision and impact for external partners and stakeholders in ways that resonate and inspire support, this position will play an integral role in helping Y-USA secure the resources needed to drive positive community change. As a member of Y-USA’s high-performing philanthropy team of talented grant writers and fundraisers, this position will bring important technical knowledge to the full grant lifecycle, from solicitation and application through fulfillment, while strengthening Y-USA’s capacity to raise and renew contributed revenue.

  • Bachelor’s degree is required. Master’s degree is preferred
  • Minimum 4-6 years of successful experience related to grant writing is required
  • Must possess a demonstrated record of success in grant writing across a variety of funding sources, public and private, as well as knowledge of the institutional funding community
  • Demonstrated superior verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills are required
  • Demonstrated superb organizational skills; diligent attention to detail; ability to manage, plan, track, and complete long-range project deadlines and goals is required
  • Demonstrated experience working well with staff at all levels and providing technical assistance is required
  • Competence across Microsoft Office Suite of programs, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, etc. is required. Familiarity with Microsoft Teams and/or other project management software, as well as visual design and formatting applications is a plus.
  • Excellent attention to detail, organizational, and customer service skills are required
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently, as well as within a team and take initiative to complete assignments is required
  • Demonstrated strong project management and problem-solving skills are required
  • Demonstrated ability to multi-task, prioritize, meet deadlines and work in a fast-paced work environment is required
  • Requires a commitment to the YMCA character development values of caring, honesty, respect and responsibility

Benefits

We offer a full benefits package including medical, dental, vision, defined benefit plan (retirement savings), defined contribution plan (403(b) plan, life and disability insurances, technology stipend, and generous paid time off, all in a work from anywhere in the U.S. workplace.

We’re hiring a PM to join our growing Life Sciences team as its second PM. You’ll own a product area end to end, working alongside our existing Life Sciences PM to shape and build products that create value for life sciences partners and health systems.

This is an early-stage opportunity with significant room to shape what we build. You’ll turn customer needs into a focused roadmap, lead discovery, and partner with engineering, ML, design, and clinical teams to bring new products to market. You’ll also work closely with business development and sales to connect product decisions to commercial outcomes.

The right person has built products for or within life sciences, brings strong product judgment, and can move from an ambiguous opportunity to a product customers use and pay for.

What You'll Do

  • Measure outcomes and iterate. Define how you’ll assess product quality, adoption, customer value, and business impact, then use evidence to improve the product.

What You Bring

  • 5+ years of product management experience, with meaningful time spent building products for or within life sciences. Pharma, biotech, medical device, or health data and analytics companies.

  • 0-to-1 experience. You’ve shipped new products.

  • Commercial fluency. You've worked closely with sales, partnerships, or BD on early-stage deals

  • Comfort with ambiguity. You're good at running discovery, forming hypotheses, and updating quickly when you're wrong.

  • Strong cross-functional credibility. You can talk to ML scientists about model outputs, to lawyers about data use agreements, and to a pharma VP about their clinical development pipeline.

  • Clear, direct communication. You write and speak well. You can take something complicated and make it simple without losing precision.

Bonus Points

  • Familiarity with how pharma companies structure and fund digital health partnerships or data licensing deals.

  • Prior work at the intersection of AI/ML and clinical data.

  • Experience with IRB considerations, HIPAA, or de-identification frameworks.

This role is a hybrid position and can be based out of our New York City office or San Francisco Office. It is 3-days in office, Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. There are no exceptions to location requirement or in-office policy.

Our mission is clear: to power deeper understanding in healthcare. We’re driving real, lasting change, with millions of medical conversations processed each month.

jobs.excerpt: Overview Brookhaven National Laboratory is seeking a highly skilled technical leader for the Applications and Software Engineering department within the Information Technology Division (ITD).
jobs.description:
Overview


Brookhaven National Laboratory is seeking a highly skilled technical leader for the Applications and Software Engineering department within the Information Technology Division (ITD). The Principal Architect provides architectural and hands-on technical leadership across multiple strategic initiatives for the Laboratory's portfolio of business applications. They will help shape the technology strategy, solution architecture, and application and platform modernization efforts that support the Laboratory's mission.


Working across a broad portfolio of legacy, custom-developed, commercial, and cloud-based applications, this role partners with business stakeholders, application architects, cybersecurity, infrastructure, and leadership to deliver secure, scalable, and sustainable technology solutions.

Reporting to the ITD Applications department manager, the Principal Architect serves as the Laboratory's technical authority for enterprise application architecture, providing strategic direction and architectural governance across the business application portfolio.

Brookhaven Lab's Information Technology Division's mission is to deliver safe, efficient operations that ensure the delivery of the Lab's research mission by:


  • Developing and deploying state-of-the-art information and computing systems in support of scientific research and business operations
  • Providing a reliable and secure, high-speed network infrastructure for scientific and business computing
  • Developing a scientific computing infrastructure that can support the computing needs common among the scientific departments
  • Providing support to scientific and administrative programs to help them address their unique computing challenges
  • Providing a cost-effective, highly reliable, secure, and standardized computing infrastructure
  • Promoting best practices in the areas of platform support, application development, and customer service
  • Providing cost-effective information services to the Brookhaven Lab community, including Research Library, publications, records management, and technical editing services, in support of the research mission and in compliance with contractual requirements
  • ITD includes experts in IT infrastructure and operations, cyber security, business systems, data information, and information services, including records management and the Research Library. The ideal candidate is an excellent communicator who is resourceful and innovative, and who understands that collaboration with stakeholders from across the Laboratory is critical to ensure the right expertise and technology are in place to advance our mission of bringing science solutions to the world.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities


  • Develop and maintain the enterprise application architecture and technology roadmaps for the Laboratory's business application portfolio
  • Lead application modernization initiatives by evaluating legacy applications, defining modernization strategies, and establishing plans that reduce technical debt and improve long-term sustainability
  • Establish and govern application architecture standards, design principles, reference architectures, and integration patterns to ensure consistency across the portfolio in partnership with the IT Architect Council
  • Review and approve solution architectures for major initiatives to ensure alignment with enterprise architecture, cybersecurity, infrastructure, data, and integration standards
  • Evaluate the application portfolio to identify opportunities for consolidation, rationalization, modernization, cloud adoption, and retirement of obsolete technologies
  • Partner with business stakeholders to translate strategic objectives into technology capabilities and multi-year business and architectural roadmaps
  • Evaluate enterprise platforms, cloud services, development frameworks, and commercial software to ensure technology investments align with the Laboratory's long-term architectural direction
  • Provide technical leadership and architectural guidance to application architects and software engineering teams, promoting engineering excellence and sound architectural practices
  • Serve as the principal technical advisor for enterprise application architecture, providing recommendations to IT leadership on emerging technologies, strategic investments, architectural risks, and technology direction

Required Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities


  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent technical experience, preferably in computer science, information systems, or a related technical field
  • 10+ years of relevant experience
  • Broad knowledge of application architecture, integrations, data architecture, identity and access management, and modern software engineering practices
  • Experience establishing architecture principles, design standards, reference architectures, and governance processes across complex application environments
  • Experience leading application modernization initiatives, reducing technical debt, and managing enterprise application portfolios
  • Strong understanding of strategic and emerging technology trends and the ability to evaluate their applicability to evolving business needs
  • Experience evaluating enterprise software, cloud services, and technology platforms to support long-term architectural direction
  • Trusted technical leader with the ability to influence executives, business leaders, architects, engineering teams, and strategic partners
  • Technology-neutral mindset with sound judgment, intellectual curiosity, and a focus on delivering sustainable business value
  • Ability to mentor architects and senior engineers
  • Applicants must submit both a resume and cover letter for consideration

Preferred Knowledge and Skills


  • 15+ years of relevant experience
  • Master’s degree in computer science, information systems, or a related field
  • Experience with ERP platforms and/or integrations such as PeopleSoft, SAP, or Microsoft Dynamics 365
  • Experience with Microsoft development technologies, including Azure, ASP.NET Core, ASP.NET MVC, Entity Framework, IIS, and Azure DevOps
  • Experience with AI-assisted and AI-integrated software development

Other information:


  • Visa Sponsorship is not available for this postion
  • This position is eligible for remote work
  • Applicants must submit both a resume and cover letter for consideration

Brookhaven National Laboratory is committed to providing fair, equitable and competitive compensation. This is a multi-level role and the full salary range for this position is $126000 - $222500 / year. You will be placed at the level and salary commensurate with your experience. Salary offers will be commensurate with the final candidate’s qualification, education and experience and considered with the internal peer group.


Brookhaven National Laboratory is committed to employee success and we believe that a comprehensive employee benefits program is an important and meaningful part of the compensation employees receive. Review more information at BNL | Benefits Program


Brookhaven National Laboratory requires all non-badged personnel including visitors to produce a REAL-ID or REAL-ID compliant documentation to access Brookhaven National Laboratory – view more information at . This is due to nationwide identification requirements for federal site access as required by the federal REAL ID Act. Those not in possession of a REAL ID-compliant document will not be permitted to access the site which includes access to the Laboratory for interviews.


As a U.S. Department of Energy laboratory, Brookhaven National Laboratory requires employees to obtain and maintain a DOE Uncleared Personal Identity Verification (UPIV) credential in accordance with Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12 (HSPD-12) requirements. The credentialing process is completed as part of onboarding and enables access to DOE facilities and information systems. As a condition of employment, the selected candidate must be able to obtain and maintain a UPIV credential. These requirements are established under DOE Order 206.2 Chg. 2, Identity, Credential, and Access Management (ICAM- Identity, Credential, and Access Management (ICAM)), and DOE Order 473.1A- Physical Protection Program- Physical Protection Program.


About Us

Brookhaven National Laboratory (www.bnl.gov) delivers discovery science and transformative technology to power and secure the nation’s future. Brookhaven Lab is a multidisciplinary laboratory with seven Nobel Prize-winning discoveries, 37 R&D 100 Awards, and more than 70 years of pioneering research. The Lab is primarily supported by the U.S. Department of Energy’s (DOE) Office of Science. Brookhaven Science Associates (BSA) operates and manages the Laboratory for DOE. BSA is a partnership between Battelle and The Research Foundation for the State University of New York on behalf of Stony Brook University. BSA salutes our veterans and active military members with careers that leverage the skills and unique experience they gained while serving our country, learn more at BNL | Opportunities for Veterans at Brookhaven National Laboratory.


Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer

Guided by our core values of integrity, responsibility, innovation, respect, and teamwork, Brookhaven Science Associates is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer-Vets/Disabled. We are committed to fostering a respectful and collaborative environment that fuels scientific discovery. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to any characteristic protected by law. All qualified individuals are encouraged to apply. We ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation. *VEVRAA Federal Contractor


BSA employees are subject to restrictions related to participation in Foreign Government Talent Recruitment Programs, as defined and detailed in United States Department of Energy Order 486.1A. You will be asked to disclose any such participation at the time of hire for review by Brookhaven. The full text of the Order may be found at:

jobs.description:
Senior Marketing Manager

Location: Remote, Canada

Niricson is transforming how critical infrastructure is inspected, understood, and managed. We combine robotics, advanced sensing, artificial intelligence, and our condition intelligence platform, AUTOSPEX, to help infrastructure owners better understand the condition of assets such as dams, bridges, and airfields. We are a global, remote-first team united by a simple mission: Making Infrastructure Safer.

The Senior Marketing Manager will build and lead the marketing engine at Niricson, and will be accountable for how the company is positioned and shows up in the market as it enters its next stage of growth.

This is not a role to simply manage social media, update our website, or coordinate marketing requests. There is an incredible amount happening across the company: new technology, global infrastructure deployments, product development, customer success stories, industry conferences, partnerships, research, and international expansion. This role will understand what is happening across Niricson, identify the stories and opportunities that matter, and turn them into a consistent market presence.

The Senior Marketing Manager will be a hands-on player-coach: setting strategy and doing some of the work directly, leading our Event & Content Manager, and, over time, deciding which roles we hire next and building the team to deliver.

THE MANDATE

Make our Sales team better at selling, our Product team better at communicating what we build, and the infrastructure industry more aware of what Niricson is accomplishing.

Key Responsibilities

The Senior Marketing Manager is accountable for results in the areas below. Some of the work will be done directly, some led through the Event & Content Manager, and some through external partners.

Marketing Strategy and Brand

  • Develop and execute Niricson's global marketing strategy.
  • Strengthen our positioning and maintain a high bar for how the company shows up.
  • Ensure consistent messaging across the website, decks, conferences, videos, case studies, and external communications.

Product Marketing

  • Work closely with Product to translate sophisticated technology into clear customer value.
  • Own product positioning, launch messaging, solution briefs, demonstrations, and competitive positioning.
  • Lead the communication of new AUTOSPEX capabilities.

Sales Enablement

  • Give our Sales team the materials they need to win.
  • Own customer presentations, pitch decks, brochures, one-pagers, videos, vertical-specific collateral, and strategic account materials.
  • Involve Sales in shaping these materials, so that Sales does not have to create them.

Customer Storytelling

  • Lead our customer storytelling program, setting priorities and quality standards.
  • Work with our content team and external creators to produce case studies, customer endorsements, videos, interviews, technical articles, and other content that demonstrates real-world impact.
  • Recognize a great story while the work is happening, not months later.

Thought Leadership and PR

  • Build a consistent content engine around infrastructure, AI, robotics, condition assessment, and asset management.
  • Proactively identify opportunities for press coverage, contributed articles, executive interviews, awards, partnerships, and industry exposure.

Conferences and Field Marketing

  • Partner with the Event & Content Manager, who leads event planning and execution.
  • Build our conference strategy with Sales and determine where Niricson should attend, exhibit, speak, sponsor, publish, or involve customers.
  • Help decide where a booth creates value, and where it does not, and ensure every priority event has a clear commercial objective.

Digital Presence

  • Own the evolution of Niricson.com, LinkedIn, newsletters, SEO, video, and other digital channels.
  • Ensure these channels consistently communicate who we are, what we are building, and why it matters.

Flagship Deployment Marketing

  • Plan ahead for important deployments and customer successes.
  • Capture the visuals, customer perspectives, technical impact, and story while the work is happening, then turn that material into high-quality sales and marketing assets.

Customer and Partner Marketing

  • Support customer expansion through product updates, customer communications, executive roundtables, joint case studies, and user events.
  • Create content that helps existing customers understand the broader Niricson and AUTOSPEX vision.

Marketing Operations

  • Build repeatable processes, calendars, metrics, templates, and standards that allow marketing to scale.
  • Manage external designers, videographers, agencies, PR resources, and specialists when needed.

Team Leadership

  • Lead and develop the Event & Content Manager.
  • Identify capability gaps and recommend the next hires or contractors to fill them.
  • Build a marketing team that can deliver routine work without depending on one person.

Decision Authority

The Senior Marketing Manager has authority to:

  • Set marketing priorities, the marketing calendar, and brand and messaging standards.
  • Approve external-facing marketing materials, including website content, collateral, and campaign messaging.
  • Select, engage, and manage external agencies, designers, videographers, and other specialists within the approved budget.
  • Recommend which conferences and events Niricson should invest in, in partnership with Sales.
  • Recommend new marketing roles and lead hiring for the marketing team.
  • Escalate pricing, commercial commitments, customer confidentiality, legal approvals, and spend outside the approved budget to the CEO.

How This Role Fits Within the Organization

This role is accountable for the marketing function. It sets the strategy, priorities, and standards for how Niricson shows up in the market. Event and content execution remain with the roles designed to own them.

  • Event & Content Manager – plans and executes Niricson’s events and conferences, and produces content within the strategy and priorities set by the Senior Marketing Manager.
  • Sales – helps shape sales materials and conference strategy, shares customer insight and opportunities, and uses marketing assets to win and expand accounts.
  • Product – owns product direction and releases, working with Marketing on positioning, launch messaging, and AUTOSPEX communication.
  • Delivery and Customer Success – involve Marketing early in flagship deployments and customer successes so stories and assets can be captured while the work is happening.
  • CEO and Leadership – set company direction and act as key voices in thought leadership, PR, and executive content.

Who We Are Looking For

You are likely someone with 7+ years of B2B marketing experience, ideally in a complex technical market such as industrial technology, infrastructure technology, engineering software, construction technology, robotics, geospatial technology, enterprise SaaS, utilities, or asset management.

You do not need to be an engineer, but you need to be curious enough to understand sophisticated technology and confident enough to turn technical conversations into compelling commercial stories.

EXPERIENCE

· Built or significantly scaled a B2B marketing function.

· Experience with complex enterprise sales cycles.

· Strong product-marketing instincts and customer-facing storytelling.

· Comfortable working with technical teams, executives, customers, and external agencies.

· Experience producing high-quality sales collateral, digital content, and thought leadership.

· Experience leading and developing marketers, and comfort as a hands-on player-coach while the team grows.

WORKING STYLE

· Can develop strategy and execute it.

· Highly proactive: you see opportunities before someone assigns them.

· Exceptional storyteller and communicator.

· High quality bar for presentations, websites, video, writing, and brand.

· Comfortable with ambiguity and a fast-moving growth environment.

· Takes ownership and measures success by business impact, not content volume.

The Trait We Care About Most

You should be able to discover the stories inside Niricson without the CEO or Sales team having to tell you every story that exists.

What Success Looks Like

Within the first year, we want to see a recognizable difference in how Niricson shows up in the market. Success is not simply more posts or more activity. It is a stronger commercial and market presence.

AREA

WHAT GOOD LOOKS LIKE

Sales enablement

Sales has current, polished materials for every priority vertical and major use case.

Customer evidence

Our strongest customer deployments consistently become credible case studies, testimonials, videos, and technical stories.

Product marketing

Major product releases have clear positioning, launch plans, and customer-facing content.

Thought leadership

Niricson develops a predictable cadence of relevant technical and executive content.

Industry presence

Priority conferences, associations, publications, and awards are approached strategically.

Digital presence

Our website and digital channels clearly communicate our technology, customer outcomes, and market leadership.

Sales impact

Marketing helps create and influence strategic opportunities and account expansion.

Executive leverage

The Senior Manager, Finance is responsible for a hybrid role combining financial planning & analysis (FP&A), business operations finance, and support for the state-specific EPR programs. The successful candidate will be a highly organized, analytical, and proactive finance leader who thrives in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment.

  • Support the Business Operations Finance Director in budgeting, forecasting and reconciling actuals verses budget, developing and improving internal tracking and external reporting processes.

  • Provide actionable financial insights and recommendations to state leadership on cash flow, revenue forecasts, cost saving opportunities, cost-benefit analyses of reimbursable system expansion investments and expense management, leveraging scenario planning and long-term projections to guide decision making.

  • Assist in ensuring compliance with state-specific EPR regulations related to financial reporting, fee collection, and producer obligations.
  • Support funding negotiations and contracting processes for state-specific EPR programs, ensuring financial transparency and proper resource allocation.
  • Prepare high-quality presentations, reports and briefings for senior leadership of CAA including Board and Committee meetings.

Skills & Competencies

  • Proven ability to understand financial modeling, forecasting, and scenario analysis.
  • Demonstrated ability to work with cross-functional teams (programs, operations, legal, compliance, communications) and support business operations in a dynamic environment.

  • Highly driven individual with a flow to work mindset and passion for navigating change and spear-heading impactful action in a fast-paced, rapidly evolving environment.

Qualifications

jobs.description:
About the role

The Solution Architect – Fiber & Structured Cabling, AI Data Center is a customer-facing technical role responsible for designing and architecting high-density fiber and structured cabling solutions for large-scale AI data center environments. The role works closely with customers, Solution Specialists, Account Executives, engineering, Professional Services, OEMs, manufacturers, and delivery teams to translate AI infrastructure requirements into scalable, repeatable, and executable physical connectivity designs. The ideal candidate brings deep expertise in data center fiber infrastructure and understands the unique density, speed, scale, quality, and deployment requirements associated with GPU clusters, high-performance networks, and hyperscale AI environments.

Annual Salary Range: $135,000 - $170,000

What you'll be doing

  • Lead technical discovery and architecture for fiber and structured cabling solutions supporting AI data center programs.
  • Translate customer compute, network, rack, and deployment requirements into physical layer designs, standards, BOMs, and implementation requirements.
  • Design high-density fiber architectures supporting GPU clusters, Ethernet and InfiniBand fabrics, storage networks, and data center interconnects.
  • Develop rack-to-rack, row, zone, meet-me-room, backbone, horizontal, and cross-connect cabling architectures.
  • Define fiber types, connectorization, polarity, patching, labeling, pathway, containment, and cable management standards.
  • Develop and validate cable matrices, port maps, connectivity schedules, rack elevations, drawings, BOMs, and installation documentation.
  • Partner with OEMs and infrastructure manufacturers to validate interoperability, standards, product selection, and technical roadmaps.
  • Support estimating, proposals, statements of work, RFQs/RFPs, technical presentations, and customer design reviews.
  • Work with Professional Services and field delivery teams to ensure designs are constructible, scalable, testable, and repeatable across large deployments.
  • Support design-to-delivery handoff, installation standards, QA/QC requirements, testing, certification, documentation, and closeout.
  • Identify opportunities to standardize and automate fiber design, documentation, BOM creation, and deployment methodologies.

What you have

  • 5+ years of experience designing fiber, structured cabling, or physical network infrastructure in data center environments.
  • Strong background in one or more AI Data Center connectivity areas, including high-density fiber architectures, GPU cluster connectivity, Ethernet/InfiniBand fabrics, structured cabling, data center interconnect, rack-level connectivity, and large-scale fiber deployment.
  • Strong knowledge of single-mode and multimode fiber, MPO/MTP and LC connectivity, polarity methods, transceivers/optics, patching architectures, and high-density fiber management.
  • Experience supporting large-scale data centers, hyperscale environments, AI infrastructure, HPC, cloud providers, NCPs, or major colocation/data center operators is strongly preferred.
  • Ability to interpret network designs, rack elevations, port maps, equipment layouts, construction drawings, and customer technical standards.
  • Experience creating or validating BOMs, cable matrices, connectivity schedules, design packages, test requirements, and as-built documentation.
  • Knowledge of structured cabling standards, installation practices, testing/certification, labeling, pathways, and data center QA/QC processes.
  • Experience working with major networking OEMs, optics providers, fiber manufacturers, and structured cabling partners.
  • Strong customer-facing communication, technical presentation, documentation, and design-review skills.
  • Ability to collaborate across sales, architecture, engineering, Professional Services, project management, operations, field delivery, and partner organizations.
  • Ability to operate in fast-moving environments where designs and deployment requirements evolve rapidly.
  • AI infrastructure and large GPU clusters
  • 400G, 800G, and emerging high-speed data center connectivity
  • High-performance Ethernet and InfiniBand fabrics
  • Hyperscale or cloud data center fiber architecture
  • High-density rack and row-level connectivity
  • Large-scale fiber installation and patching programs
  • Pre-terminated and modular fiber solutions
  • Offsite fiber preparation, kitting, labeling, and pre-integration
  • Fiber testing, certification, troubleshooting, and remediation
  • Automated cable matrices, BOMs, port mapping, and design documentation
  • Multi-site deployment standards and repeatable data center design methodologies
  • Fiber Architecture – Deep understanding of high-density data center fiber design and physical connectivity.
  • AI Infrastructure Knowledge – Understands how GPU compute, networking, storage, and rack architectures drive physical layer requirements.
  • Design at Scale – Creates repeatable architectures capable of supporting thousands of racks and very large connection counts.
  • Technical Accuracy – Maintains rigorous attention to port mapping, polarity, labeling, testing, documentation, and quality.
  • Customer Engagement – Can lead technical discovery, design workshops, and customer architecture reviews.
  • Design-to-Delivery Thinking – Develops solutions that can be efficiently sourced, pre-built, installed, tested, and operated.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration – Connects customer requirements with sales, engineering, sourcing, partners, and field delivery.
  • Quality and accuracy of fiber and structured cabling designs
  • Speed from customer requirements to executable solution architecture
  • Design standardization and repeatability across AI Data Center programs
  • Reduction of field changes, rework, and connectivity defects
  • Successful technical support of pipeline and customer pursuits
  • Accuracy of BOMs, cable matrices, port maps, and design documentation
  • Successful transition from solution architecture into deployment
  • Customer satisfaction and technical credibility
  • Continuous improvement of fiber design and deployment methodology
  • The ideal candidate is a hands-on data center fiber architect who understands how to turn complex AI infrastructure and network requirements into highly accurate, scalable physical connectivity solutions. They should be comfortable working from GPU and network architecture down to the rack, port, optic, fiber, connector, pathway, and patching level.
  • This individual should combine strong technical depth with practical deployment experience—someone who can design for scale while understanding how the solution will actually be sourced, staged, installed, tested, documented, and supported in a high-velocity AI Data Center environment.

What you can expect

There’s so much more to enjoy about being at Computacenter than just having a rewarding career. In addition to offering competitive compensation plans and long-term career opportunities, we provide an attractive mix of benefit plans to contribute to your good health, future financial security, and peace of mind.

About us

Computacenter is a leading independent technology partner, trusted by large corporate and public sector organizations. We help our world-renowned customers to source, transform, and manage their IT infrastructure to deliver digital transformation, enabling users and their business. We’re a public company quoted on the London FTSE 250 (CCC.L) and employ over 21,000 people worldwide. In the US, we support some of the country’s best-known businesses with regional hubs in San Francisco and Irvine, CA; Norcross, GA; Plano, TX; and New York City; and Integration Centers in Silicon Valley and Atlanta.

jobs.title: Revenue Operations Support Analyst
jobs.excerpt: About KojoIt's time to build.  Whether it's creating more housing, upgrading our infrastructure, or adapting to climate change, one thing is clear: the construction industry is at the center of solving our biggest problems.
jobs.description:
About Kojo

It's time to build. Whether it's creating more housing, upgrading our infrastructure, or adapting to climate change, one thing is clear: the construction industry is at the center of solving our biggest problems. We’re making buildings cheaper and easier to build by transforming the way commercial construction companies buy their materials. Join us.

Founded in 2018, Kojo is now one of the fastest-growing construction technology companies in the world. Construction accounts for $10 trillion in global spend annually and we can’t live without its output - our roads, schools, hospitals, and offices. Despite this, there’s been very little innovation over the past 70 years in how materials - which constitute up to 40% of project costs - are bought and sold. This is our opportunity.

About the Role

Kojo's Sales and Customer Success teams run on Salesforce, and when something in that world needs a hand — a quote that has to be built by hand, an account that needs to move, a duplicate that needs merging, a report that doesn't add up — the request lands in one queue. You'll be the first person to pick it up.

The most important part of the job is custom quotes. Most agreements go out on a standard template a rep can send alone. The ones that don't — a mid-term expansion co-termed to an existing subscription, a split payment schedule, a multi-year deal paid upfront, a contract that has to list every module with its own dates and price, an amendment to something already signed — come to you. You'll get the opportunity and quote right, generate the order form, edit it where the template can't, and get it out through DocuSign, quickly and correctly.

Around that core you'll work the rest of the RevOps queue: account ownership and routing changes, duplicate merges, small Salesforce fixes, data questions, and tool questions. You'll report to the Revenue Operations Coordinator, and the two of you will run the queue together — you resolving what can be resolved directly, escalating what needs deeper Salesforce work, and both of you turning the patterns you see into fixes so the same request stops coming back.

Commercial decisions — pricing, discounts, non-standard terms — belong to the go-to-market organization, Sales and Customer Success. Your role is to make sure what they've agreed is captured accurately, approved where it needs to be, and reflected exactly in what the customer signs and in Salesforce afterwards.

What you'll own

  • Efficiently shipping custom quotes and order forms. This is the most important part of your role. Take a rep's request — a co-term with a prorated amount, a custom payment schedule, a one-time fee on a multi-year term, a multi-entity or module-level contract, an entity or start-date change, a rider or addendum, a credit — and turn it into a correct opportunity, quote, order form and DocuSign envelope. Same day where the deal needs it. Work with the RevOps Coordinate to iterate SFDC and DocuSign to accelerate our ability to ship an accurate quote. You ensure the GTM team is focused on the customer and not the critical CRM data we need to onboard, recognize revenue, and bill customer accurately.

  • Quotes and DocuSign when they misbehave. Diagnose why a generated agreement came out wrong — quote not syncing, billing or shipping details missing, products missing or duplicated, a price not reading through, no signature field, a Closed Won that won't save — work with the revenue operations coordinator to identify how SFDC should be updated, and / or show the rep how to avoid it next time.

  • The approval layer. Understand Kojo’s deal policies and how they show up in the SFDC deal flow. Keep approval status accurate, and confirm the right approvals are in place before an envelope goes out.

  • The rest of the queue. Account ownership and routing changes, inbound credits, duplicate account and contact merges, picklist and field tweaks, user access issues, renewal record discrepancies, cancellation processing, and answering questions about RevOps-owned tools, and knowing which tools are not owned by RevOps and routing the question to the owner of that tool. Triage fast, resolve what you can, escalate cleanly, and keep the requester informed.

  • The record after signature. Make sure term dates, amounts, products, and credits in Salesforce match the signed agreement to the day, that the renewal opportunities that should exist do exist, and that cancellations and amendments leave clean data behind.

  • Making requests disappear. Spot the recurring patterns in the queue and create business requirements to reduce the incidence of the recurring pattern in the future. Work with the Coordinator who will perform the configuration and development work to turn those business requirements into a template fix, a field, a validation rule, a small flow, or a how-to that lets reps self-serve.

About You

What we're looking for:

  • Revenue operations or deal desk experience: 2+ years at a B2B SaaS company in a seat where quotes, orders, or Salesforce requests came to you — deal desk, sales operations, revenue operations, order management, or Salesforce support.

  • Hands-on in Salesforce: you're fluent in the Opportunity → Quote → Product data model, comfortable with reports, list views, and bulk updates, and you've made real configuration changes — fields, picklists, validation rules, page layouts, simple flows — in an org other people depended on. Salesforce Administrator certification, or experience that clearly stands in for it.

  • DocuSign beyond the send button: templates, merge fields and tabs, routing, reminders and expiry. Experience with DocuSign for Salesforce or Gen for Salesforce is a strong advantage.

  • Contract math as a reflex: prorations, co-terms, day counts, split payment schedules, multi-year totals — and the habit of stating your convention before your number.

  • Precision with documents: you can edit an order form in Word so the language, table, and totals are exactly right, and you notice when they aren't.

  • Precise written English: you'll write to reps, CSMs, and customers all day. Spoken English sufficient for a daily working session with the team.

  • A queue temperament: organized, quick to acknowledge, quick to close the loop, and able to tell a rep at quarter-end that a document isn't ready yet — with the reason and the fastest path forward.

  • Based in Latin America, with at least four hours of daily overlap with US Central time and flexibility in the final week of each quarter.

Nice to have:

  • Admin exposure to the GTM tools around Salesforce — Chili Piper, Outreach, ZoomInfo, Gong.

  • Exposure to how a signed contract becomes an invoice (Stripe or another billing platform).

  • A recurring manual request you turned into a template, automation, or how-to — and what it removed.

  • Experience supporting construction, manufacturing, or another industrial market.

What you care about

  • Accountability: when an order form goes out wrong or a record doesn't match the paper, you treat it as yours to fix — and then you fix the reason it happened.

  • Impact: you sequence the queue by what unblocks a deal and what protects a customer relationship, not by what arrived first.

  • Intentional Communication: you write with the right context and no ambiguity — to a rep who's stuck, a CSM mid-renewal, or a customer reading an order form.

  • Collaboration: you check with the rep, the CSM, and the Coordinator before you build, so the contract that goes out is the one everyone thinks went out.

Working at Kojo

Salary: Your salary will be dependent upon many factors, including your experience level, skillset, market dynamics and balancing internal equity relative to other Kojo employees. The compensation and benefits information that we provide is based on Kojo’s good-faith estimate as of the date of the job posting and may be modified in the future.

Benefits: This position is also eligible for a new hire equity grant and all US-based full time employees are eligible for our full suite of perks and benefits. For more information about our perks and benefits, check out

Location: Kojo’s team members work from home 100% of the time across North and South America. If applicable, we’ll identify the travel and/or location-specific requirements of a position in the text above. Otherwise, team members can expect to work business hours congruent with their local time zone and remotely.

Inclusive Workplace: Kojo values diverse perspectives and is committed to building an inclusive workplace. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and do not discriminate on the basis of sex, race, color, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, national origin, citizenship, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. We strongly encourage people from underrepresented groups to apply.



Scam Notice: Please be aware that there are individuals and organizations that may attempt to scam job seekers by offering fraudulent employment opportunities in the name of Kojo. These scams may involve fake job postings, unsolicited emails, or messages claiming to be from our recruiters or hiring managers. Kojo will never ask for any personal account information, such credit card details or bank account numbers, during the recruitment process.

jobs.title: Bridge Design Engineer (Projektant Mostów)
jobs.excerpt: WSP jest wiodącą na świecie firmą inżynieryjną, specjalizującą się w infrastrukturze, transporcie, ochronie środowiska, energii i budynkach.
jobs.description:
WSP jest wiodącą na świecie firmą inżynieryjną, specjalizującą się w infrastrukturze, transporcie, ochronie środowiska, energii i budynkach.

Mamy jasną wizję tego, w jaki sposób chcemy pomóc uczynić świat lepszym miejscem, wspierając społeczności i to, co jest naprawdę ważne dla naszej przyszłości.

Wyobraź sobie lepszą przyszłość dla nas wszystkich - i lepszą przyszłość dla Ciebie.

Do naszego zespołu Infrastruktury poszukujemy Projektanta Mostów.

Będziesz uczestniczyć w realizacji projektów mostowych i infrastrukturalnych dla rynków skandynawskich, współpracując na co dzień z zespołami WSP w Szwecji i Finlandii. W tej roli będziesz brać udział w opracowywaniu dokumentacji projektowej, analizie i modelowaniu konstrukcji oraz przygotowywaniu rozwiązań technicznych dla złożonych inwestycji infrastrukturalnych.
Możliwość pracy zdalnej lub hybrydowej w naszym biurze w Warszawie lub w Krakowie.

Twoje zadania

  • Projektowanie obiektów mostowych oraz opracowywanie obliczeń i modeli konstrukcyjnych 3D.

  • Analiza i dobór rozwiązań technicznych, materiałów oraz technologii budowlanych.

  • Opracowywanie i weryfikacja dokumentacji projektowej oraz optymalizacja rozwiązań projektowych.

  • Przygotowywanie przedmiarów robót i wsparcie procesu realizacji projektów.

  • Współpraca z zespołami projektowymi WSP w Szwecji i Finlandii.

  • Koordynacja projektów z innymi branżami oraz udział w spotkaniach projektowych.

  • Współpraca z klientami, podwykonawcami i interesariuszami projektu.

  • Dbanie o terminową realizację powierzonych zadań oraz wysoką jakość opracowań projektowych.

O zespole

Dołączysz do zespołu infrastrukturalnego WSP, który realizuje projekty mostowe i transportowe dla klientów w Polsce i za granicą. Współpracujemy na co dzień z zespołami WSP w Szwecji i Finlandii, wykorzystując nowoczesne narzędzia projektowe oraz środowisko BIM.

Projektujemy nowe obiekty mostowe, modernizacje istniejącej infrastruktury oraz opracowujemy rozwiązania wspierające optymalizację kosztową inwestycji. W swojej pracy korzystamy m.in. z programów SOFiSTiK, Robot Structural Analysis, BRIGADE, Mathcad, Tekla i Revit.

Wybrane projekty

  • Östlänken (Szwecja) - jedna z największych inwestycji kolejowych realizowanych w Szwecji.

  • Klara City View (Sztokholm, Szwecja) - projekt wielobranżowy realizowany w centrum Sztokholmu.

  • Most Kirjalansalmi (Finlandia) - jeden z najbardziej rozpoznawalnych projektów mostowych realizowanych przez WSP w Finlandii.

Kogo szukamy?

Niezbędne kwalifikacje

  • Wykształcenie wyższe techniczne w zakresie budownictwa, preferowana specjalność mostowa.

  • Doświadczenie w projektowaniu obiektów mostowych i infrastrukturalnych.

  • Znajomość polskiego prawa budowlanego, norm i standardów branżowych.

  • Umiejętność rozwiązywania problemów technicznych i analizowania rozwiązań projektowych.

  • Komunikatywna znajomość języka angielskiego.

  • Bardzo dobra znajomość AutoCAD oraz innych programów CAD.

  • Dobra znajomość pakietu Microsoft Office (Word, Excel).

Mile widziane

  • Znajomość programów Revit, Tekla lub SOFiSTiK.

  • Doświadczenie w pracy w środowisku BIM.

  • Doświadczenie przy projektach międzynarodowych.

Co oferujemy?

  • Rozwój w międzynarodowym biurze projektowym

  • Możliwość realizacji prestiżowych projektów

  • Opiekę medyczną

  • Dofinansowanie do karty Multisport

  • Dostęp do platformy wellbeing (w tym 5 bezpłatnych konsultacji z psychologiem, prawnikiem i/lub doradcą finansowym rocznie)

  • Dofinansowanie lekcji językowych, kursów i szkoleń

  • Możliwość pracy zdalnej

Nasz proces rekrutacji:

  • Analiza CV.

  • Krótka rozmowa telefoniczna z rekruterem.

  • Spotkanie online lub w biurze z kierownikiem zespołu.

  • Możliwe dodatkowe spotkanie techniczne.

Pracuj z WSP.

Z nami możesz.

#WeAreWSP

Recognized as a global leader in subscription commerce, Infiterra combines innovation, performance excellence, and trusted expertise to help partners transform and grow.

About The Role

As a Senior AI Engineer, you will be part of R&D and will design, build, evaluate and operate production AI systems that solve meaningful product and engineering problems.

This is an Applied AI Engineering role combining deep AI specialization, strong software engineering and business/domain understanding. You will work across LLM-based systems, retrieval, agents, tool use, predictive techniques and model adaptation/fine-tuning where appropriate - choosing the approach based on the problem and evidence rather than defaulting to one AI technique.

You will take complex AI capabilities end-to-end: from understanding an ambiguous business problem, through experimentation and solution design, to implementation, evaluation, deployment, monitoring and continuous improvement.

This is a fully remote senior individual-contributor role based in either Greece or the UK, with periodic in-person collaboration.

Our AI engineering environment includes Python, cloud-native services, containers/Kubernetes, CI/CD, model APIs, retrieval and agent/tool frameworks, and evaluation/observability tooling. We choose technologies based on the problem rather than standardizing on one AI framework.

What You Will Work On

  • AI-native product engineering and knowledge systems that reconcile business knowledge from product, engineering and production evidence.

  • Automated and reusable vendor-integration capabilities, including the evolution of our Integration Hub from implementation automation toward learning from real integration outcomes.

  • AI-assisted software delivery: analysis, requirements, implementation, testing, knowledge reuse, code review and delivery acceleration.

  • AI-enabled quality and production intelligence, such as anomaly detection, failure-pattern analysis, data-quality/error detection and intelligent monitoring.

  • Predictive, analytical or model-adaptation capabilities where evidence shows they are the right solution.

What Success Looks Like

In your first 90 days, you will have developed a strong understanding of our platform and domain, contributed materially to a production AI capability, established meaningful evaluation evidence around your work, and identified opportunities where AI can create measurable product or engineering leverage.

By six months, you will independently own one or more complex production AI systems or workflows - evaluated, observable and operationally reliable - and will have introduced reusable technical knowledge or practices that improve how the wider engineering team builds with AI.

Success is not measured by the number of AI features introduced. It is measured by business correctness, AI behavioural quality, engineering quality, production reliability and demonstrated value.

Who You Are

You are comfortable being given a business problem rather than a detailed technical specification. You can experiment quickly, but you also do the harder engineering work required to make AI behaviour measurable, reliable and maintainable in production. You understand that AI output is not automatically truth, make assumptions and limitations explicit, and design evaluation and human controls according to risk. You are equally comfortable discussing model behaviour, APIs and distributed-system failures as you are understanding the business rules the system is expected to support.

Responsibilities

  • Own the design, implementation, evaluation and production operation of complex AI systems involving multiple components, integrations or workflows.

  • Translate ambiguous business problems, rules and domain constraints into measurable AI/system behaviour.

  • Build production systems using model APIs, structured outputs, retrieval/RAG, agentic and tool-based workflows, predictive techniques and other appropriate AI patterns.

  • Design evaluation strategies covering functional behaviour, groundedness, business correctness, robustness and regressions.

  • Engineer for reliability, testability, observability, maintainability, latency and cost.

  • Design production learning loops and determine whether behaviour should be improved through context, retrieval, orchestration, model choice, adaptation/fine-tuning or other techniques.

  • Identify and validate AI-enabled improvements to SDLC, Product and operational workflows.

  • Explore AI-enabled platform-quality capabilities such as anomaly detection, data-quality/error detection, failure-pattern analysis and intelligent monitoring where they provide measurable value.

Qualifications

  • AI systems: Strong hands-on experience delivering production AI systems; model APIs, structured outputs, tool-based systems, retrieval/RAG, agentic workflows, predictive techniques and model adaptation/fine-tuning where appropriate; able to select the appropriate AI approach based on problem context and evaluation evidence.

  • Evaluation: Experience designing behavioural, groundedness/business-correctness, robustness and regression evaluations, including production evaluation, monitoring and feedback loops.

  • Engineering: Strong software-engineering background, particularly Python; distributed systems, APIs, integrations, data pipelines, automated testing, CI/CD, containers/cloud and production-grade engineering practices.

  • Production: Strong observability and production troubleshooting skills including logs, metrics and traces; reliability, testability, latency/cost awareness and complex failure investigation.

  • Business/domain: Ability to understand complex workflows, business rules, dependencies and constraints and translate ambiguous business problems into reliable system behaviour.

jobs.description:
about us:

Spectrum.Life is a whole-of-health digital partner that guides organisations and their people to thrive, delivering clinically backed digital health, mental health and wellbeing solutions.

Our HealthTech delivers digital transformation for Insurers, Educators and Employers through Co-creation or seamlessly integrated out-of-the-box solutions, that decrease digital fragmentation and engage, empower, and transform their people’s lives.

Established in 2018 by Stuart McGoldrick and Stephen Costello, Spectrum.Life provides services internationally to over 7.2m insurance members, 3,000 corporate clients, 60 universities and 650,000 university students. Spectrum.Life currently employs over 450 people.

Our vision is to change and save as many lives as possible.

role brief:

The role of Adult, Children and Young People’s Digital Psychotherapist is suited to fully qualified and fully accredited psychotherapists. The Adult, Children and Young People’s Digital Psychotherapist is a key part of the Spectrum clinical team, providing access to evidence-based talking therapies to adults, children and young people, such as integrative psychotherapy pulling on techniques such as CBT and Goal Based Intervention (GBI) as clinically appropriate. Sessions are for adults aged 18 and over and for children and young people aged 6 to 17, last up to 50 minutes, are delivered online, and are booked through the member platform once our 24/7 clinical team has completed clinical triage and activated the service. Minimum of two to three years of post-qualification experience working with adults and children, adolescents, and families

responsibilities:

  • Provide goal-focused therapeutic support to adults, children, adolescents, using age- and developmentally appropriate interventions to address a range of emotional and psychological difficulties, including anxiety, depression, trauma, grief and complex presentations.
  • Conduct a comprehensive assessment at the start of each episode of care, building on the clinical triage completed by our 24/7 clinical team, to identify the individual's needs, developmental stage (for children and young people), risk factors, and protective factors, ensuring appropriate intervention strategies.
  • Deliver evidence-based psychological interventions, including but not limited to:
    • Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT) for anxiety, depression, and trauma.
    • Dialectical Behaviour Therapy (DBT) skills for emotional regulation and self-harm reduction.
    • Play Therapy and Art Therapy for younger children with attachment or developmental needs.
    • Family-Based Interventions (FBT, Systemic Therapy) for eating disorders, behavioural challenges, and family distress.
  • Provide immediate crisis interventions through telephone or video support, including risk assessment, suicide prevention strategies, and emotional regulation techniques.
  • Assess and manage risk effectively, identifying and escalating concerns related to self-harm, suicidal ideation, abuse, neglect, or exploitation in line with child protection procedures, adult safeguarding procedures and safeguarding policies.
  • Follow safeguarding protocols by recognising, reporting, and responding appropriately to child protection and adult safeguarding concerns, liaising with relevant agencies (e.g., TUSLA, education, and law enforcement).
  • Determine the appropriate service response level based on the severity and complexity of the individual's presenting difficulties, following case response level standards.
  • Work collaboratively with families, caregivers, and educational staff, where appropriate, to provide psychoeducation and support strategies that reinforce therapeutic goals.
  • Recommend liaison with multidisciplinary teams (MDTs), including social workers, psychiatrists, teachers, GPs, and other healthcare professionals, ensuring a holistic approach to care.
  • Maintain accurate, professional, and confidential clinical records, adhering to GDPR, service policies, and ethical guidelines for data protection on our internal clinical case management system.
  • Engage in research, evaluation, and clinical audits to support service development and ensure the continuous improvement of therapeutic outcomes.
  • Operate within all clinical governance frameworks, policies, and procedures, ensuring compliance with regulatory standards and ethical guidelines.
  • Attend clinical supervision, safeguarding training, and CPD activities to maintain high standards of practice and stay updated on emerging evidence-based practices.
  • Contribute to service development and expansion, working on projects related to improving mental health provision for adults, children and young people, including digital innovations and accessibility.
  • Advocate for the needs and rights of adults, children and young people, ensuring interventions are inclusive, neuroaffirmative, culturally sensitive, and trauma-informed.
  • Deliver online sessions of up to 50 minutes to adults aged 18 and over and to children and young people aged 6 to 17 who have been triaged by our 24/7 clinical team and who book directly into your diary once the service has been activated for them.
  • Keep your availability up to date so that first appointments can be offered within 10 working days of clinical activation, in line with our agreed service levels.
  • For children and young people, work within our child and adolescent pathway, in which parental or guardian consent is embedded, and ensure consent is documented before therapy begins.
  • Apply our cancellation and missed-appointment policies
  • Make informed clinical decisions, including modality, session frequency and discharge, within our clinical governance framework.

requirements:

Essential Qualifications and Registration:

  • Full accredited membership with one of the following:
    • Irish Association for Counselling and Psychotherapy (IACP)
    • Irish Council for Psychotherapy
    • British Association of Behavioural and Cognitive Psychotherapy
    • Irish Association of Behavioural and Cognitive Psychotherapy
    • Chartered with Psychological Society of Ireland (PSI)
  • A clean record with the associated regulatory body
  • Accreditation and Training – Meets IACP requirements for working with adults and children, including:
    • Specialist training in child development, play therapy, systemic therapy, and legal aspects of child counselling.
    • Understanding of psychopharmacology relevant to the mental health of adults, children and young people.
    • Experience in practical, supervised training with children and adolescents.
  • A clean record with the associated regulatory body.
Essential Experience:
  • Experience and interest in working with adults, and with children and young people aged 6 to 17 years
  • Multidisciplinary Collaboration – Experience working with social workers, CAMHS, schools, and healthcare professionals to ensure holistic care.
  • Culturally Sensitive and Neuroaffirmative Practice – Experience working with diverse populations, including neurodivergent clients, LGBTQ+ youth, and children from different cultural backgrounds.
  • Innovation in Digital Mental Health – Experience in digital or hybrid therapy models, ensuring accessibility for clients of all ages.
Essential Knowledge and Skills:
  • Evidence-Based Interventions – Proficiency in delivering developmentally appropriate psychological integrative therapies, including:
    • Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT)
    • Dialectical Behaviour Therapy (DBT) skills
    • Goal Based Interventions (GBI)
    • Play Therapy and Art Therapy
    • Family-Based Interventions (FBT, Systemic Therapy)
  • Child and Adolescent Development – Strong understanding of typical and atypical development, attachment theory, and neurodevelopmental conditions.
  • Crisis Intervention and Risk Management – Ability to assess and manage crisis situations, including self-harm, suicidal ideation, abuse, and neglect.
  • Child Protection and Safeguarding – In-depth knowledge of child protection laws, policies, and procedures, including the Children First Act and GDPR, and of adult safeguarding procedures.
  • Consent and Confidentiality – Understanding of legal and ethical responsibilities regarding consent and confidentiality for under-18s, including:
    • Parental/guardian consent processes
    • Contracting with families for therapy
    • Limits of confidentiality in safeguarding situations
  • Mandatory Reporting – Ability to identify, document, and escalate safeguarding concerns appropriately.
  • Clinical Governance and Record-Keeping – Adheres to professional and ethical guidelines, including GDPR, clinical documentation, and service policies.
  • Commitment to Continuous Professional Development (CPD) – Engages in regular CPD, supervision, and training to maintain accreditation and ensure best practice.
  • Building Rapport with Adults, Children and Adolescents – Skilled in adapting therapeutic approaches to meet the needs of each individual, including developmental needs.
  • Working with Families and Caregivers – Ability to provide psychoeducation, support strategies, and involve caregivers in the therapeutic process.
  • Research and Evaluation – Contributes to service audits, clinical evaluations, and outcome measures for continuous service improvement.
  • Multi-Agency Liaison and Advocacy – Advocates for the needs and rights of adults, children and young people, ensuring accessible, effective, and ethical care.
  • Strong understanding of clinical governance, GDPR, and safeguarding procedures.
  • Ability to work independently while contributing to a multidisciplinary team.
  • Ability to work afternoons and evenings,
  • Good computing skills: Microsoft software (e.g., Word, Excel, Teams), email, internet, video conferencing software, and clinical record-keeping software (we use Salesforce), including approved AI-assisted clinical transcription tools.
Values and Behaviours:

In addition to professional competency, the Adult, Children and Young People’s Digital Psychotherapist is expected to demonstrate the following:
  • Person-centred practice — keeping the voice, rights and wellbeing of the adults, children and young people we support at the heart of every decision, and advocating for them.
  • Commitment to psychological safety — creating conditions where adults, young people, families and colleagues can ask questions, raise concerns and disclose errors without fear of judgement.
  • Equity and inclusion — active attention to the needs of diverse populations, and neuroaffirmative, culturally sensitive and trauma-informed practice.
  • Data literacy — using outcome data and feedback as genuine quality improvement tools.
  • Collaborative practice — working openly with families, schools, the multidisciplinary team and partner agencies.
  • Commitment to the evidence base — maintaining fidelity to NICE guidelines and professional accreditation standards, and exercising independent clinical judgement within clinical governance frameworks.

  • The opportunity to work in a strengths based and inclusive way and contribute to a bigger shift in changing societal attitudes towards mental health and wellbeing
  • Remote supervision
  • Opportunities to develop your skills and expertise through learning and training
  • The chance to contribute to the development and shaping of a new and exciting service
  • Extensive list of employee perks and benefits
